title: Heron's Formula OQ-04: Triangle Isoperimetric Inequality

problemStatement.formal: For positive side lengths a, b, c satisfying the triangle inequalities, Heron's product s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c), with s = (a+b+c)/2, is at most s^4/27.
problemStatement.plain: Uses Heron's formula and the three-variable AM-GM inequality to prove that, among triangles with a fixed perimeter, the equilateral triangle maximizes area.
whyMatters: This is the classical triangle isoperimetric inequality in a form directly tied to Heron's area formula.
The proof exposes reusable AM-GM and equality-case lemmas for later geometry entries.
The quantitative perimeter bound gives a searchable theorem-level endpoint instead of a placeholder description.

proven: `amgm_three_nonneg` proves the three-variable AM-GM inequality for nonnegative real inputs.
`amgm_three_eq_iff` records the positive equality case for the AM-GM step.
`heron_product_le_equilateral` bounds Heron's product by the equilateral triangle with the same perimeter.
`heron_product_eq_equilateral_iff` identifies equality with the equilateral case.
`triangle_area_sq_le` and `isoperimetric_ratio` package the area and perimeter forms of the triangle isoperimetric inequality.
`HeronsFormulaOQ04.lean` is recorded with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.
open: General polygonal isoperimetric results and the cyclic-quadrilateral analogue are outside this OQ-04 metadata slice.
knownResults.goal: Make the theorem-backed Heron/AM-GM proof of the fixed-perimeter triangle area bound searchable.
